title: The Holy Congregation in Jerusalem
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: In Berakhot 9b: Rabbi Yose ben Elyakim testified in the name of the Holy Congregation in Jerusalem that whoever juxtaposes the redemption blessing to the prayer, etc. And in Rosh Hashanah 19b: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi testified in their name.

And in Beitzah 14b, 27a: Rabbi Shimon ben Pazi said, Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said, Rabbi Yose ben Shaul said: Rabbi said in the name of the Holy Congregation in Jerusalem. Hyman suggests they were called this because, from the destruction of Betar onward, no Jew was permitted to enter even the area of Jerusalem; nevertheless the exalted pious ones risked their lives and dwelt secretly in Jerusalem (without doubt they bribed [the authorities] on their behalf), and engaged in Torah and prayer. Therefore they called them the Holy Congregation, since they were exposed to the sword at all times. But they are not connected with the 'Holy Community' as explained in its entry.

notes.text: The cause of the name, secret residence and supposed bribery are Hyman’s own conjecture. This congregation is expressly distinguished from Edah Kedoshah, the “Holy Community.”
